races.name: Twilight Racing On The Dee Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Country Park
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with two wins over course and distance on good ground, making him the most credible late challenger, but 44 days off and a fall earlier in his recent form string inject slight uncertainty about jumping sharpness; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is a key booking at this track.

runners_data.name: Lermoos Legend
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old handicapper fitted with a tongue-strap and cheekpieces who runs from off the pace, back quickly after just 10 days and with a modest recent record of two wins from 15 similar-ground starts; the short turnaround and age make a bold showing against younger rivals a stretch.

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Three-from-three at the front over good ground and stepping back up in distance after a 63-day break, with hood and tongue-strap suggesting he can be enthusiastic — uncontested lead is a golden opportunity to extend his winning run and the Donald McCain yard has been active with 13 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Duel Au Soleil
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling's six-year-old has placed on good ground on four of his last five starts and maps to track the leader in second or third, giving him a straightforward racing position; the step back from the softer conditions of his last run looks a positive and his 51-day break leaves him fresh enough to sustain a challenge.

runners_data.name: Disco Davis
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' seven-year-old has modest recent form including two pulled-up runs and no wins on similar ground from eight attempts; he will race prominently and give James Best a platform, but the raw data offers little encouragement at this level with a 69-day absence compounding the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Jiair Madrik is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, controlled gallop from the front over 2m4½f on good ground at Bangor. Duel Au Soleil and Disco Davis are both prominent-style horses who will track up close, likely occupying second and third early, but neither has the profile to actively challenge for the lead — they will simply ensure the pace isn't dawdling without forcing a war. Country Park and Lermoos Legend are hold-up horses who will be consigned to the back two early, relying on a strong late run over a course and distance that genuinely tests stamina. With Jiair Madrik setting a fair, metronomic clip unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-leading types who can control the contest and kick clear at their own rhythm — true hold-up horses face the double burden of ground covered at a sustainable pace and a track that rarely produces dramatic late swoops.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jiair Madrik Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik leads without pressure and converts his hat-trick of wins into a front-running display under Theo Gillard.
scenarios.body: Jiair Madrik has won his last three starts from the front and faces no credible threat to his lead here, allowing him to set a rhythm that blunts the closers' finishing speed. On good ground over this trip, a confident, controlling front-runner with fresh legs (63 days off) is the dominant profile, and Duel Au Soleil is best placed of those tracking him.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik sets too hot a pace or makes a jumping error that allows Duel Au Soleil or Disco Davis to sweep through from close range.
scenarios.body: Duel Au Soleil, with solid good-ground form (1W5P on similar) and a strong second most recently over this distance, is ideally mapped to track and pounce if the leader cracks, while Disco Davis has the physical profile to stay in contention from a tracking role. Ben Jones on Duel Au Soleil represents a capable partnership for this type of assignment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Runs On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and one of the hold-up horses finishes with a sustained rattle up the home straight.
scenarios.body: Country Park arrives on the back of two wins over this course and distance on good ground and represents the most credible late threat from the rear, having shown the ability to quicken off a sound pace at Bangor. Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is an astute judge of pace and could time a run perfectly if the front two fight each other harder than expected, though the forecast scenario makes this a secondary outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Jumping Errors Reshuffle
scenarios.trigger: If one or more horses make costly jumping mistakes that disrupt the race order and produce an untidy, stop-start contest.
scenarios.body: Lermoos Legend, a hold-up 11-year-old meeting this trip fresh from a 10-day turnaround, could benefit from a scrappy race that neutralises front-running supremacy, and Country Park's earlier fall in form (F in recent form) is a reminder that jumping can always intervene. An untidy race opens the door to experience and robustness over raw pace.

watchPoints.text: Jiair Madrik's jumping — three consecutive wins from the front have been built on clean rounds, and any fence error under Theo Gillard on the final circuit would immediately invert the race result in favour of Duel Au Soleil or Country Park.

Disco Davis's jumping reliability is a live concern given two pulled-up finishes in recent form; racing prominently from an inside position, a mistake could cause interference to Duel Au Soleil or disrupt the rhythm of the chasing pack.

Lermoos Legend's very quick 10-day turnaround for an 11-year-old steeple chaser over a longer trip than his last start warrants monitoring early — if he fails to travel fluently from off the pace, he could become a rearward nuisance at the fences.

Country Park's course-and-distance record on good ground (2 wins from a strong sample) is the most compelling late-race narrative to track — if the early pace is genuine enough to soften up Jiair Madrik by the home turn, watch whether Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is able to find daylight wide on the run-in.

races.name: John Hewitt Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Roadlesstravelled
runners_data.note: OR 132 class horse for Jonjo O'Neill Jr. and the joint-yard, but 80 days off the track is a concern for sharpness; front-runs boldly and has the rating to dominate if fresh, though the recent form string of PP finishes after that early sequence of wins warrants caution.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Sean Quinlan partner for Jennie Candlish has a superb 13/15 record on Good ground and five wins at the trip, finishing in the frame in all five recent starts; tongue-strap in use, ran just 19 days ago staying sharp, and the prominent-but-not-lead style is perfectly suited to a pace war erupting ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Krak
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton partners this Dan Skelton runner (yard in 7/20 T14 form) who has posted consistent placed efforts on Good ground but has yet to convert any of those four near-misses into a win; front-runs in the hood and will have to compete for the lead against two other confirmed pace horses, which risks a messy early battle.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: 70-day absence for the Sarah-Jayne Davies yard (0/3 T14) adds a fitness question mark; front-runs on Good ground with three wins from ten similar-going starts, but competing for the lead against Roadlesstravelled and Krak at OR 113 — the lowest in the field — makes winning from the front a tall order.

races.paceDynamic: Roadlesstravelled, Krak, and Ice In The Veins are all confirmed front-runners in a field of just four, meaning the early gallop at Bangor will be fierce and unrelenting from the off. One of the three will ultimately boss the lead — Roadlesstravelled is the class act of the trio at OR 132 with Jonjo O'Neill Jr. likely to assert early, but Krak (Harry Skelton, in-form yard) and Ice In The Veins will not surrender ground without a fight. The resulting strong pace over 2m1½f on Good ground will test stamina hard and compress finishing margins, burning through the field's reserves before the final fences. This race shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent-to-handy horse with a proven stamina base and the tactical nous to track the war without joining it — making Captain Cool the profile that should benefit most, as the sole non-front-runner able to sit just off a genuinely hot gallop and pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War; Captain Cool Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Roadlesstravelled, Krak, and Ice In The Veins burn each other off up front, leaving Captain Cool to cruise into contention.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners drive a punishing early gallop that saps their collective stamina, and Sean Quinlan on Captain Cool can switch off just behind before producing a measured challenge at the final fence. Captain Cool's exceptional Good-ground record (13/15 in similar conditions, 5 wins) and proven ability over this trip marks him as the prime beneficiary of an honest pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Roadlesstravelled Controls; Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Roadlesstravelled's class advantage allows him to dictate a controlled front-running display rather than an all-out dogfight.
scenarios.body: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. settles Roadlesstravelled at a manageable lead while Krak and Ice In The Veins are covered up or fade, and the OR 132 raider simply outclasses the field jumping and staying. The 80-day break is a watch point, but Jonjo O'Neill's yard comes into this with a live runner and Roadlesstravelled's form peak suggests no obvious regression.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Krak Finds Rhythm; Skelton Masterclass
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Skelton allows Krak to bowl along in a lead role at his own pace, with the Skelton yard's 7/20 T14 form providing a fit horse ready to fire.
scenarios.body: Krak's five runs over Good ground show consistent placed form and he handles the trip, and if the pace war fails to fully materialise — with Ice In The Veins tiring early — Krak could find a clear lead and grind out a performance. However, Krak's zero wins from four placed runs in similar conditions is a caution against over-weighting this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Ice In The Veins Stuns; Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ice In The Veins bounces fresh off a 70-day break, leads strongly, and the field fails to reel her in over the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Her three wins from ten Good-ground starts show she's capable, and if Roadlesstravelled and Krak both produce below-par efforts, the Davies-trained mare could front-run to a surprise victory. This remains the least likely outcome given she is the lowest-rated runner and has previously faded badly when the pace pressure increased.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Roadlesstravelled actually secures the lead over Krak and Ice In The Veins in the opening half-mile — whoever controls the front end will dictate whether this becomes an even-tempo grind or a chaotic speed duel.

Krak's attempt to front-run in a three-way pace battle could see Harry Skelton forced to make a decision early: fight for the lead and risk blowing up, or drop in behind and race against his natural style.

Ice In The Veins returns from 70 days off for a trainer with 0/3 over the past fortnight — any race-rustiness at the first fence or two fences will be immediately exposed given the pace she'll be asked to travel.

Captain Cool wore a tongue-strap today and ran just 19 days ago — watch the pre-race market move as any drift could indicate the quick turnaround has left a mark, but a hold or shortening confirms the stable's confidence in his fitness.

With only four runners, any jumping errors early — especially from the front-running trio — could dramatically reshuffle the order and hand Captain Cool a free passage into contention without even having to improve.

races.name: Paul Ferguson's Jumpers To Follow Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Cadillac Ranch
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win last time out (Good, 20f) and solid sim-going record (1W1P from 2); Miss Ellie Callwood's 7lb claim helps carry the weight, and at just 11 days since last run this horse arrives fresh and likely to push hard for the lead from flag-fall.

runners_data.name: Provision
runners_data.note: Won last time on Good ground over 16f and carries strong Irish novice form, but Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim suits the yard; her natural style is hold-up and she will find it harder than usual to settle in her preferred rear position given the number of hold-up types in this field — treat a prominent-map position with caution and expect her to be towards the back half.

runners_data.name: Hidden Fortune
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's string is firing (7/20 T14) and Harry Skelton takes over, which is always significant; this 5yo front-runner has won on Good ground and placed on Soft, and after 117 days off the track the fitness question is the only caveat against a horse whose profile screams race-shaper.

runners_data.name: Pretty Darn Quick
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the bottom half of fields on Good and Soft, flagged as a fader in the finish, and absent 87 days; her true racing style is hold-up but the crowded rear section means she is mapped to midfield — a style-fit discount applies, and her OR of 73 leaves her outclassed in this company.

runners_data.name: Ride Like A Girl
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden's mare has excellent Good-ground credentials (2 wins from 6 sim-going runs) and the step from 16f to 21f looks well within range given her stamina-laden profile; Gavin Sheehan will be eyeing a prominent pitch just off the front pair, and her recent form string (344-12) shows she is coming into her own.

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: Donald McCain runner (T14: 0/13, a cold stable) which tempers enthusiasm despite a solid sim-going placings record (2W6P from 15 runs); the horse arrives on 37 days' rest wearing headgear and brings strong flat-track speed, making her a genuine prominent player if the yard finds its form.

runners_data.name: Rose Warrior
runners_data.note: A 4yo who managed only an 8th on debut over hurdles on Good ground and whose Flat form on Standard ground is modest; the headgear (hood, p=first time in this context) is worth noting, but fading finishes are a pattern and Ian Power faces a stiff task from what may be the worst profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Evenly
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners this McCain runner, but the yard is cold (0/13 T14) and form readings of 60 over 16f on Good are uninspiring; only 2 career runs in the book, both without placing, and a 20-day turnaround for a horse rated 147 suggests connections may just be looking for experience.

races.paceDynamic: Cadillac Ranch and Hidden Fortune are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over 2m½f on Good ground at Bangor, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a dawdle. Hidden Fortune (Harry Skelton, Dan Skelton yard in T14 form at 7/20) is likely to be the more assertive of the two given class and connections, while Cadillac Ranch will push for the rail and apply pressure throughout the early and middle portions of the race. Secret Beach and Ride Like A Girl will sit prominently just behind the front pair, meaning the race will have a solid, honest tempo from flag to finish — this shape strongly favours horses that can travel fluently in a rhythm and pick off a tiring leader in the straight, giving the edge to well-placed prominent types with proven Good-ground form. This field holds more hold-up horses than can realistically settle at the rear — Provision and Pretty Darn Quick are genuine hold-up types pushed into midfield on the map, but with the pace genuine and the track's relatively flat Bangor layout, Ride Like A Girl and Secret Beach are best placed to exploit the shape from a prominent position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Gut It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Hidden Fortune and Cadillac Ranch set an honest but controlled gallop and one kicks clear from the front two furlongs out before the others can respond.
scenarios.body: The contested early pace gradually strings the field out, and the stronger galloper of the two front-runners finds a second gear that the prominent chasers cannot match on Good Bangor ground; the Skelton handler's record (7/20 T14) suggests Hidden Fortune is fit, sharp and primed to dominate from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other off sufficiently that a well-placed prominent runner swoops past the final hurdle with momentum to spare.
scenarios.body: Ride Like A Girl has an excellent Good-ground profile at this trip (6/8 sim-going placings, 2 wins) and Gavin Sheehan will have her sitting a length or two off the lead ready to capitalise the moment the duelling front-runners weaken; Secret Beach's flat track Flat background gives her the speed to quicken past tiring rivals in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to leave the front-runners and prominent horses spent inside the final furlong, gifting a late closer the spoils.
scenarios.body: Provision is the most likely beneficiary — a winner on Good ground and well-handicapped stepping up in trip — though the redistribution note means she is likely further back than ideal and will need a very strong pace to bridge the gap; Evenly and Rose Warrior are too lightly-raced or form-weak to be relied upon in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Race
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners refuse to commit and the pace collapses into a falsely-run affair that produces a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow-run race over 2m½f on Good ground scrambles the form book and could allow an unexposed runner like Secret Beach — with strong Flat speed and headgear applied — to quicken fastest in a dash; Pretty Darn Quick is out of role and flagged as a fader, making this scenario's outcome particularly unpredictable and its likelihood low given both Cadillac Ranch and Hidden Fortune's confirmed front-running profiles.

watchPoints.text: Hidden Fortune and Cadillac Ranch will lock horns for the lead from the start — watch whether either blinks and concedes, because whichever secures the rail and dictates pace without a fight will have a materially better chance of lasting home.

Secret Beach carries the flag for a cold Donald McCain yard (0/13 T14) but has strong speed and headgear applied — if the stable suddenly fires, she is the most dangerous uninvited guest in the prominent group and could be significantly shorter in the ring than form suggests.

Provision is a legitimate winner on this going but will likely end up three or four lengths further back than her natural style requires given the log-jam of hold-up types — watch her run-in position; if she threads through to challenge early in the straight she is live, but a tardy clearance from the rear will cost her the race.

Pretty Darn Quick is flagged as a fader with a style-fit discount and a substantial absence (87 days) — if she travels surprisingly well into the straight ignore the profile note, but in any normal unfolding of this race she is best used as a pace-indicator rather than a win candidate.

Rose Warrior's headgear switch (first time hood noted as 'p') is worth monitoring in the market — first-time headgear can spark improvement in novices, and while her form reads poorly, an unexpected market move would warrant a second look at her stamina profile for this 21f trip.

races.name: Wrexham Lager Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Who's Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Donald McCain who has placed twice on good ground at this distance; 91 days off is notable, and his best recent finishes have come at 20f rather than this 19f trip, so stamina is not the concern — freshness and early tactical positioning are.|

runners_data.name: Person of Interest
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden's presence is the key angle here — an obvious jockey upgrade for Faye Bramley's improving six-year-old who has won twice and placed five times in fifteen good-ground runs; ran 11 days ago in a competitive heat and is clearly in a purple patch.|

runners_data.name: Rock Hurley
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over this course and distance on his last winning start; Mr Harry Brown claiming 10lb is a factor, but tongue-tie reapplied and a proven record of 1W/2P from five similar-going runs gives him a live chance if allowed to dictate at his own pace.|

runners_data.name: Lunar Orbit
runners_data.note: Strong form at a young age for the Skelton yard — 7/20 in the last fortnight speaks to trainer confidence — but this horse is a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of rear runners; its STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) means it is unlikely to get a clean sit in behind as intended.|

runners_data.name: Zamond
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran for Donald McCain who is a genuine prominent racer, the most structurally suited profile in this race shape; 2W/7P from twelve good-ground runs is a consistent record and a 10-day turnaround from a second-place finish shows he is in form.|

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse for Brian Ellison who has won twice on good ground but is likely to be displaced from his natural position by the congestion at the rear; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.94) means he may end up closer to the pace than ideal, which historically has not brought out his best.|

runners_data.name: Auntie Maggie
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will contest early leadership with Rock Hurley; her recent form reads 3-52P4 and she has dropped to OR 90 after her pull-up, making it hard to see her sustaining a pace duel over 2m3½f — likely to be the one that burns bright and fades.|

runners_data.name: Cappa Lass
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with no wins or places in four good-ground starts; ran just four days ago which is a very quick turnaround, and as a hold-up type mapped to midfield through redistribution, she faces both a positional and a form challenge in this company.|

races.paceDynamic: Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off, creating a genuine, honestly-run gallop over 2m3½f on good ground at Bangor. Rock Hurley, who won over this course and trip last time and carries a tongue-tie back on, is likely to assert as the controlling leader, with Auntie Maggie pushing him along from his outside and keeping the tempo honest throughout. Zamond is the only genuine prominent-racing type and will sit just off the two leaders, ideally placed to pounce if the front pair tire; the hold-up horses — Who's Glen, Person of Interest, Lunar Orbit, Dream Jet and Cappa Lass — will be further back, though the field carries more rear-of-field types than the race shape can naturally accommodate, meaning Lunar Orbit, Dream Jet and Cappa Lass are unlikely to find their ideal hold-up berth. This contested, genuine-gallop shape on good turf structurally favours a prominent racer with a strong cruising speed who can track the pace and produce a clean jump at the last, making Zamond's profile and Zamond's record of five place efforts from twelve good-ground starts the most naturally suited.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Zamond Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie fight out a genuine gallop that stretches the field, leaving Zamond to travel comfortably in third before asserting from two out.
scenarios.body: Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie burn each other off at a true pace, and Zamond — who has placed in seven of twelve similar-going runs — has just enough left to collar the tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If Rock Hurley, tracking a rhythm he knows well at this course and trip, controls the pace without being seriously harried and sustains his effort to the line.
scenarios.body: Rock Hurley won here last time over this course and distance and his tongue-tie is back on; if Auntie Maggie fades early he can set a comfortable gallop and prove hard to catch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or softens sufficiently in the home straight to allow a late-closing run from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Person of Interest has the best recent good-ground form of the hold-up runners with two wins and five places from fourteen similar-going efforts, and Harry Cobden gives a significant jockey upgrade; Who's Glen has placed in this grade on good ground but needs a genuine test to get home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners set an unsustainable early tempo and both capitulate, turning the race into a scramble from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: A muddled finish could see a hold-up type get the run of the race; Lunar Orbit and Dream Jet are genuine hold-up horses racing out of their natural position here, and their chances are tempered by the crowded rear.

watchPoints.text: Rock Hurley and Auntie Maggie will duel for the lead from the off — watch whether Auntie Maggie cracks early or pushes Rock Hurley into an unsustainable gallop, as the answer will define the entire shape of this race.

Person of Interest is on a quick 11-day turnaround with a top jockey booking; if Harry Cobden navigates him into a position just behind Zamond rather than deep in the rear, his good-ground record makes him a significant danger late.

Zamond ran just 10 days ago and is a 10-year-old; watch whether Theo Gillard can hold him up slightly behind the two leaders rather than getting sucked into a battle — if he does, his prominent profile is the most structurally suited in this race.

Cappa Lass ran four days ago and is a hold-up horse in a race with too many hold-up horses; monitor whether Toby Wynne drops her out completely or tries to push forward, as either way she faces an awkward race shape.

Lunar Orbit's yard is 7/20 in the last 14 days and the Skelton team rarely run out of form without intent; watch the market for any late move that suggests they have found a tactical solution to the crowded rear of the field.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse with strong course-and-distance credentials on Good turf (three of last five over 16f on Good), and Stuart Edmunds' runner has a genuine profile for this trip; 52 days off is unremarkable but the trainer's 14-day record of 0/3 warrants mild caution.

runners_data.name: Eremenko
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's front-runner carries the STYLE_FIT flag, a reminder that his 0.92 fit score means any disruption to his position could undermine his chance; however, with no other confirmed leader in the field, he is likely to secure the rail and dictate, and his 1/20f Good win demonstrates he stays the trip.

runners_data.name: Roarin' Success
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back winner (1-1 in last two) gives this McCain-trained six-year-old solid form claims, and a prominent style should allow Theo Gillard to sit just off Eremenko and apply late pressure; the 9/15 sim-going record is respectable rather than exceptional.

runners_data.name: Uhtred Ragnarson
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old is in truth a hold-up horse whose natural closing run is compromised by the crowded rear of this field — Tom Cannon may find his passage restricted; the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.91 and a mixed recent form string (3-F-7-3-5) do not help his cause at a tight, turning track.

runners_data.name: Playful Fox
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old arrives in the best recent form of the field (U24121, with two wins in last three completed outings), and Harry Skelton's booking is a significant positive; a hold-up style with a strong sim-going record (7/9) suggests this horse travels well enough to sit a touch closer than pure closers if needed.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's consistent handicapper — placed in four of last five on Good or similar — is a genuine hold-up type whose natural style is squeezed by the number of closers in this field, leaving Alex Harvey (3) needing fortune in running on a tight circuit; the OR of 96 leaves the widest margin to exploit if everything clicks.

races.paceDynamic: Eremenko is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Roarin' Success likely to press from a prominent position, he should secure the lead without serious contest and control a sustainable, measured gallop around Bangor's tight track. Roarin' Success will sit close behind, creating a two-horse front group while the remainder are held at bay in the early stages. The field actually contains more hold-up types than can naturally find the rear — Uhtred Ragnarson and Syosset are true closers pushed into the midfield mapping because the back of the field is already crowded, meaning they may not get the clean, late run their style demands. This race shape — a single controlled front-runner setting a genuine but unforced pace over 2m½f on Good turf — strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or close smoothly from mid-division, with the hold-up horses facing the additional hurdle of navigating traffic on a turning track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eremenko Controls, Stays Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Eremenko dictates an uncontested, honest gallop and neither prominent challenger has the reserves to reel him in from the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Eremenko, freed from pressure, settles into his own rhythm and the consistent pace is just strong enough to anchor the hold-up horses without giving them a sprint to aim at; Roarin' Success, drawn into a prominent duel for second, is best placed to pounce if Eremenko fades.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Roarin' Success pushes Eremenko hard from the turn and the race becomes a two-way battle that opens the door to a closing run.
scenarios.body: A contested pace between the two McCain-trained horses raises the tempo enough to leave both vulnerable in the closing stages, and a horse tracking them in third or fourth — most likely Playful Fox or Hello Sweety — swoops late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the closers find a clean passage up the home straight to deliver a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Hello Sweety has the course form and Playful Fox the recent winning momentum to exploit this, but Uhtred Ragnarson and Syosset, though genuine hold-up types in reality, are mapped out of their natural position and may not get the unobstructed run this scenario demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Race Produces Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle of the race and every runner is bunched turning for home, producing a messy finish decided by jockeyship.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton on the in-form Playful Fox and Brian Hughes on Eremenko are the most likely beneficiaries of a chaotic scenario given their ability to quicken and dictate positioning mid-race; Syosset's consistency in place positions could earn minor honours.

watchPoints.text: Eremenko's ability to dictate unchallenged is the pivotal factor — watch whether Roarin' Success's early stride puts him under pressure before the halfway point, as any sustained duel between the two McCain horses fundamentally changes the race shape.

Playful Fox is the most in-form runner in the field and Harry Skelton's aggressive positioning ability means this horse could travel closer than its hold-up label suggests — watch where Skelton slots him in the first three furlongs.

Uhtred Ragnarson and Syosset are genuine rear-runners who may struggle to find daylight on Bangor's turning track — if both are trapped in traffic at the top of the straight, neither can fulfil their role and their chance evaporates quickly.

Tom Cannon's record at Bangor and his management of Uhtred Ragnarson's position in the early stages is worth tracking — if he is forced wider or further back than ideal, flag it as a significant disadvantage for the horse's scenario.

runners_data.name: Fane Court

races.paceDynamic: Camino Rocio and Seahouses are the two confirmed front-runners here, and with both likely to press forward from the outset over 2m7f on Good ground, an honest, competitive gallop is the probable outcome rather than a dawdle. Camino Rocio brings Harry Skelton in the saddle and a recent run under her belt (16 days), giving her a meaningful edge in terms of freshness and jockey quality at the front, while Seahouses — 142 days off the track and ridden by a 5lb claimer — faces more questions about her ability to sustain that pressure through the final mile. The genuine pace they generate over this staying trip will string the field out and test resolution from the fourth hurdle onwards, strongly favouring horses that can race prominently without being consumed by the early duel, or those disciplined enough to travel sweetly just off the pace and pick up the pieces late. The field contains more hold-up horses than can genuinely settle at the rear in this shape — You Did and Fine Print are both true hold-up types that have been mapped to midfield positions because Hillview and Present Fair already occupy the back of the field; in practice, those two may struggle to find their natural rhythm if they are pushed further forward than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Camino Rocio and Seahouses fight out a genuine duel and the pace is honest throughout, setting up a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop burns off the hold-up horses who cannot fully settle and rewards the horse travelling smoothly just off the two leaders; Scottish Dancer, with good form on Good ground over a comparable trip and a prominent style, is ideally placed to pounce jumping the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Camino Rocio Dictates Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Seahouses fades or fails to press Camino Rocio early, leaving her to control tempo and conserve energy through the final circuit.
scenarios.body: Camino Rocio has Harry Skelton dictating from the front and a strong recent trainer strike rate (T14: 7/20), and on Good ground — going she handles well (11/15 sim-going) — she can quicken clear off her own fractions when not pressed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front two burn each other out badly enough to open the door for a late finisher who has conserved energy through the early chaos.
scenarios.body: Hillview and Present Fair are the genuine hold-up operators here, and both handle Good ground; Present Fair's winning form at 2m3f Good and Hillview's similar-going record (1W5P) give each a platform if the race falls apart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Seahouses fades dramatically early and Camino Rocio is left alone with nothing to run against, causing the pace to drop and set up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A steadier early gallop compresses the field and makes the race a stamina test in name only; Fane Court, who has placed in his last three and stays this trip consistently, would be equipped for a tactical affair from a prominent position.

watchPoints.text: Camino Rocio vs Seahouses early: watch whether Seahouses (142 days off, 5lb claimer) can genuinely match Camino Rocio for the lead or capitulates inside the first mile, which will determine the entire pace shape.|

Scottish Dancer's trip history: his last four runs before this were over 12-16f, making the jump back to 2m7f a stamina query despite his excellent Good-ground record — watch how he travels as the race enters the final circuit.|

You Did and Fine Print out of position: both are natural hold-up horses likely to race in midfield rather than their preferred spot at the rear; if the pace is genuinely strong, they may be caught in no-man's land and unable to deliver their finishing kick.|

Hillview at 10 years old: a decade-old horse with a patchy recent string (P7-7P5) requiring an unusual amount of things to go right — monitor market support to gauge stable confidence on first run from Gary Hanmer since returning.|

Fane Court's quiet progression: three consecutive placings and Kielan Woods booked make him interesting under the radar; if the market firms him beyond his OR of 80, it may signal yard confidence in a horse who handles this distance and ground reliably.|
